messages:
maya: Quick sync — I want to propose changing the admission semantics for the elastic-stripe allocator. Current behavior ties admission tokens to a fixed probe window (20s) which causes bunching when lots of tenants probe at the same cadence. Thinking of moving to a jittered, lease-based admission with a soft headroom watermark and a short probe cooldown.

ryan: Can you sketch the leases vs probe cooldown interaction?

maya: Sure. Idea: when a tenant is allowed a slot we grant a lease (e.g., 30–90s) instead of a one-shot token. While lease active, tenant can open concurrent requests up to its slot limit without re-probing. If it stops sending traffic, lease naturally expires. Probes only occur after cooldown to avoid stampeding.

jun: Sounds promising. How do we handle eviction ordering when capacity tightens? Lease age? recency? priority class?

maya: Eviction order = (preemptible flag, priority class, lease_score), where lease_score blends remaining_time and historical throughput. So fresh hot tenants are less likely to be evicted than long-idle ones that held a lease but didn't use it.

sophia: My worry: SLOs for low-latency-tier customers. If we give leases too long we may underutilize and miss latency targets for high-tier requests. Any guardrails?

maya: Agreed. We add two controls: 1) a per-pool soft_headroom % that keeps X% capacity unleased for on-demand low-latency traffic; 2) a fast-evict path that can rescind leases for a small percentage of slots when an SLA-critical request shows up (with observable fallback to lower-cost variants).

ryan: Example config sketch for the policy DSL:

```
policy: elastic_stripe_v2
lease: min=30s, max=90s, jitter=0.2
probe: cooldown=45s, jitter=0.5
soft_headroom: 12%\npreempt_path: on_sla_request -> rescind_leases(limit=5%)
metrics: emit {lease_grant, lease_revoke, probe_rate, headroom_fill}
```

ryan: (obvs rough)

sophia: That helps. For rollout — we should dark-launch metrics and then canary on a dedicated pool with lower risk. Also add regression alerts on p50/p95 latency and admission_fails.

maya: Rollout plan: 1) feature-flagged dark metrics for 2 weeks, 2) canary in dedicated stage pool at 10% traffic, 3) expand to low-risk tenant cohorts with automatic rollback on 3x baseline alert rate.

ops-bot: snapshot: pool-stats@2026-02-14T10:12Z headroom_fill=31%, probe_rate=420/s, active_leases=278

zach: Need to tie active_leases to billing tags — otherwise we under-attribute reserved cost on monthly reports. Also consider making lease_duration influence amortized cost buckets.

maya: Good call. We'll emit lease_start/lease_end with tenant tags to billing stream. Also add a periodic reconciler job to decrement unused leases for cost accuracy.

maya: Action items: @ryan plumb metrics into the observability dashboard (lease_* + headroom_fill). @jun prototype eviction scoring function and open a small perf bench. @sophia draft SLA escalation playbook for fast-evict path. @zach add billing mapping. I'll draft an RFC update with config DSL and rollout checklist. +1s or concerns? :thinking_face:"
